subtopic: Caring for a sick parent while studying
subtype: Approach: notice signs of caregiver fatigue and step back [Revision]
passage:
Tanvir hadn't slept properly for three weeks. In the noisy ward, with one week left before the exam, he snapped at a nurse over a small thing, then apologised too many times. On the bus he realised he had been irritable every single day, and that the bad sleep never lifted.

He thought about it that evening. It isn't one bad day. It's the whole pattern. He called his Dilnaz khala and said, "I can't keep doing every night. Could you take two of them?" She said yes before he finished.

The next morning he booked a counselling session at the college. It was hard to admit, but the care he gave Dad had been getting sharper, and that was the real signal.

qa.q: How many nights did Tanvir ask Dilnaz khala to take?
How was Tanvir feeling as he snapped at the nurse and then apologised too many times?
qa.a: Tanvir was exhausted and ashamed, and the constant irritation and poor sleep made him see that he was worn out.

qa.q: What could Tanvir do on the nights off, and why?
qa.a: Tanvir could sleep and revise in a quiet place away from the ward, because rest helps both his exam and his patience when he returns.

qa.q: How might Dilnaz khala feel about being asked?
qa.a: Dilnaz khala said yes before Tanvir finished, so she probably felt glad to be asked and was worried he had carried so much alone.

grounding: Realising that irritation and poor sleep are constant, the student asks an aunt to take two nights and books a counselling session.

passage:
Usha noticed it at the medical shop in Kolkata's Salt Lake market. The chemist gave her the wrong change, and she heard herself snap at him. On the walk back she realised she had snapped at three people that day, including her father, who had only asked what time it was.
She had not slept properly in weeks. She woke at every sound from his room.
That night she called Masi. "I need help. Could you stay here two nights a week, maybe Wednesday and Saturday?" Masi said she'd come on Wednesday.
Then she opened the college wellbeing page and booked a counselling session for Friday. She told her friend Suraj, who had been asking for weeks why she looked so tired.
On Wednesday she slept nine hours in her own room with the door shut. In the morning she made her father's tea and actually listened to his long story about the neighbour's cat.

qa.q: Which nights did Usha ask Masi to stay?
qa.a: She asked Masi to stay Wednesday and Saturday.

qa.q: What was Usha feeling on the walk back from the medical shop?
qa.a: She felt worn out and shaken, noticing she had snapped at three people that day, including her father.

qa.q: What else could Usha do after the counselling session?
qa.a: She could keep the two Masi nights fixed and review with the counsellor whether more help is needed, so the rest doesn't slip away again.

qa.q: How might her father experience the change?
qa.a: Her father gets a calmer daughter who listens to his stories instead of snapping, which likely makes him feel more at ease.

grounding: Shows the student noticing constant irritation and poor sleep while caregiving, asking an aunt to cover two nights and booking counselling.

"You shouted at the pressure cooker," Disha said from the doorway.
Naveen stopped. "It whistled too early."
"You shouted at the cooker, at the delivery man and at me. All before ten." His sister sat on the kitchen stool. "When did you last sleep through?"
He rubbed his eyes. "Before Amma's surgery. I keep waking to check on her."
"And you're angry all the time."
"I know." He leaned on the counter. "I keep thinking it's just a bad week. It's been six."
Disha waited.
"Okay," he said finally. "I'll call Chitti. She offered before. I'll ask her to take Tuesday and Friday nights." He picked up his phone. "And the college counsellor has slots on Thursday. I'll book one now."
"Now now?"
"Now now." He booked it and showed her the screen. Then he turned off the cooker and apologised to it, which made Disha laugh.

qa.q: Which nights did Naveen plan to ask Chitti to take?
qa.a: He planned to ask her to take Tuesday and Friday nights.

qa.q: How does Naveen feel when Disha lists who he shouted at?
qa.a: He feels tired and a bit ashamed, admitting he knows he is angry all the time and that it has been six weeks, not one.

qa.q: What else could Naveen do to keep the care sustainable?
qa.a: He could set a regular check-in with Disha every week about how he is sleeping, so the warning signs are noticed early next time.

qa.q: How might Disha feel when Naveen books the session in front of her?
qa.a: Disha is likely relieved and a bit amused, laughing when he apologises to the cooker after taking a real step.

grounding: Shows the student realising constant anger and poor sleep are warning signs, asking an aunt to take two nights and booking a counselling session.
